## Goal

Make TreeDB's external-timestamp MVCC an efficient substrate for Dgraph posting reads and sustained updates. Reuse the fastest existing source-selection, ordered-seek, batch and ownership paths before building new machinery. Done means the admitted changes have their own correctness/performance proofs, the matched TreeDB/Badger gap narrows under a frozen measurement policy, and obsolete version history is reclaimed with bounded maintenance and foreground disruption.

Execution authorized by the repository owner in the current Codex session: /root coordinates, revises the graph, assigns isolated issue worktrees and owns merges. All delegated implementation workers, finalizers, advisers and independent reviewers use requested `gpt-6.1-sol`; actual served identity is not separately exposed. Hosted quota/service unavailability is a typed unavailable gate, with an exact-head independent Sol fallback only where repository policy permits; it is not a review pass. Do not request credit-consuming reviews before the local packet is mature. Publishing the original plan was tracking-only; this subsequent instruction authorizes execution through validation and merge under the existing gates. The final evidence owner for this graph is [M9](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4879). Existing [snissn/dgraph#34](https://github.com/snissn/dgraph/issues/34) retains durable coalescing and its historical promotion gate.

## Verified base and evidence

Planning base: Gomap main `7fd6cbcf802dc1a2df86b9e7073eda509307dc36`; Dgraph main `0a08775fef51b4c6920934a268081e9472f44890`. Source inspection used Gomap runtime-equivalent lock-fix worktree `c72171685a3ca8fb2054ae79269a799450e52d03`; Dgraph retained adapter blob `33a86ee482a61731c3db34bf90b692ca9b4016bd` matches live main. Earlier dependency-only runtime commits are provenance, not public source links. Refresh the assigned implementation bases.

| Evidence | Observed result | Interpretation / boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-optimization current-machine 3-repeat, 2k-timed matched matrix | relaxed: Badger 11,166.60 vs TreeDB 8,436.81 ops/s; durable: 1,957.63 vs 708.62 | Historical baseline for #4862; not post-lock-fix current parity |
| Merged [#4868](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/4868), five 20k pairs per mode | relaxed +1.80%; durable +21.31%, durable p50 +16.62% tradeoff | Measured read-lock repair; 30s timer created differing checkpoint counts |

Original ~3.44 audit used a different denominator/window. Read-cut causality remains to be measured. |

Runtime/profiling attribution uses the artifacts linked in [#4862's live ledger](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4862#issuecomment-5923843537) and [#4868's qualification packet](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/4868#issuecomment-5926083273). Exact local audit paths are retained in the original tracker; each new child must publish its own reproducible evidence rather than inheriting an improvement claim.

## Architectural findings and ownership

| Static finding | Implementation / decision owner | What must be proved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Posting all-version reads acquire a physical snapshot that can rotate every mutable shard | [M4](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4875), measured by [M0](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4872) | Stable physical source cut, fewer irrelevant rotations/tiny publications, bounded pin lifetime |
| Exact-key iteration uses generic synthetic bounds and all-source merge despite existing shard affinity | [M1](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4873) and caller [M3](https://github.com/snissn/dgraph/issues/36) | Canonical exact range, relevant shard only, tombstone/range/source precedence |
| Non-exact timestamp successors can scan/sort large mutable maps; backend pin is eager on queue candidates | [M5](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4876) | Actual production eligibility and bounded search/pin cost; historical no-land controls |
| Multi-record commit holds Store.mu through WriteSync | [M6](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4877) | Complete-group visibility without fencing readers for WAL wait; not a measured singleton bottleneck |
| Iterator Entry/point decoding can copy owned payloads repeatedly, and forward seek/history selection does avoidable work | [M2](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4874) and [M3](https://github.com/snissn/dgraph/issues/36) | Explicit ownership/lifetime, equivalent required posting chain, fewer copies/visits |
| Production advances discard floor without scheduling physical version prune; current qualified prune is a whole-scan fence | [M7](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4878) and [M8](https://github.com/snissn/dgraph/issues/37) | Durable floor before deletes, no resurrection, bounded quantum, eventual reachability reclamation |
| Small publication units and ordered durable tickets retain per-request cost | [M4](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4875) for read-cut amplification; existing Dgraph #34 for coalescing | Distinguish publication work from WAL/fsync, naturally queued independent work; no invented linger |

The review supports these mechanisms, not a whole-MVCC rewrite or a claim that every one explains the current timed gap. Old versions are real index/value-log roots; the value log is persistent storage, and physical segment deletion remains reachability-based.

## Gates and failure actions

| Gate / metric | Class | Current | Target / boundary | Failure action / owner |

| Durability-matched TreeDB throughput relative to Badger, both modes | North-star | Old pre-fix gap measured; fresh matched current gap not yet established | Repeated gap reduction beyond the noise/improvement threshold frozen by M0; throughput/tail policy declared before candidates | M9 and parent stay open; attribute and link one owned next limiter |
| Exact-key source/copy/cut work | Child exit gates | Mechanisms above; current normalized costs measured by M0 | Each child moves its own declared path/work target through the production caller | Owning child stays open; do not accept helper-only success |
| Bounded pruning and required live/pinned retention | North-star safety/maintenance gate | Whole-scan qualified fence; no production prune orchestration | Quantum bounds scanned work/foreground fence, progress completes, live/pinned history preserved | M7/M8 block final gate; no automatic deletion without proof |
| ACK, atomic visibility, floor ordering, reopen/recovery, reachability, ownership | Hard guardrails | Existing contracts/tests | Preserve all required invariants; changed durable-owned bytes receive appropriate evidence | Fix before merge; performance cannot waive correctness |

M0 is accepted and closed. The sole current default-off reference is Gomap28aea01e / clean dependency-only Dgraph eaf5a2ab. Relaxed Badger11600.47/TreeDB9193.95 ops/s; durable1828.93/691.51. The parent target is more than10% relative improvement in each median TreeDB/Badger ratio plus every predeclared aligned repeat ratio improving, with fixed5% unexplained tail/CPU and10% RSS/endpoint-disk guardrails. Exact numerical medians, every repeat, resource scopes and hashes are in the [accepted M0 packet](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/issues/4872#issuecomment-5930339397). Native promotion remains STOP; no parity/promotion waiver. M4/M5/M6 are NO-GO implementation now, open/inactive with revisit triggers; availability counters are not elapsed cost. The architecture candidate cannot widen these thresholds after measurement.

## Documentation, allocation and PR policy

Preflight read: root and `TreeDB/AGENTS.md`; spec index; `contracts.md`; write-path section 5.3; concurrency admission; recovery section 4.4; value-log lifecycle section 2.2; verification MVCC/conformance; storage-format pre-alpha policy; Gomap CONTRIBUTING and optimization PR template; Dgraph CONTRIBUTING and PR template; both repositories' live default-branch rules. Source/caller facts are pinned in each child.

Reusable primitives: canonical MVCC codec/affinity, shard-local published-root metadata, retained memtable/root views, existing owned and borrowed iterator surfaces, BTree/sorted-run seeks, atomic raw batches, command-WAL durable tickets and the persisted floor/oldest-first prune algorithm. Actual eligibility/fallback is proved before replacing these. Avoid a second transaction engine, new WAL, blanket pooling, unsafe zero-copy or a new timestamp index without measured necessity.

Each behavior-changing child owns its canonical docs, API/example guidance, test-first regression or explicit exception, B/op/allocs/op and actual routing/materialization/fallback proof. Retention/capture changes include live/retained memory. No extra process, tests-only or docs-only milestones; pure instrumentation/artifact nodes have explicit test-first exceptions. Default generic paths remain checked as guardrails. Owned outputs count as legitimate allocations; avoidable repeated copying is minimized before closure.

Durable means stable dependency-complete command-WAL prefix plus publication, without forcing a backend checkpoint. Relaxed command-WAL ACK includes kernel draining and publication without fsync, not a userspace-only memtable ACK. Persistent value-log GC is always reachability-based. Recovery docs contain broader historic batch/relaxed statements that M0 must reconcile with the profile-specific contract before descendants consume them.

Gomap: current main requires a PR, current base and `TreeDB required gate`; non-fast-forward pushes are prohibited. Human approval is not newly imposed (live required count is zero). Use coherent topic branches, focused and broader affected tests, appropriate race/recovery checks, mature review and current-head CI. Copilot automatic review is configured; quota unavailability is a typed absence, not acceptance. The template's blanket provider fields do not require purchasing every provider review. Dgraph follows its PR/lint/test policy; no live rules were returned at inspection. Refresh both before actual implementation/merge. The stale `docs/OPT_SPRINT_NEXT.md` template pointer is not an invented gate; current canonical docs and harness own the evidence.

## Ownership review and required corrections

- M0 consumes #4862’s accepted final matrix only after checking exact runtime/harness closure and comparison policy. Its first new packet is direct snapshot-cut accounting plus a bounded public exact-key iteration fixture; existing stats/profiles are reused. Additional successor or multi-record probes require a discriminating question.
